findings.description: Collision cleanup deletes agent-added production modules anywhere in the tree, even though basename collisions only matter for particular pytest imports. Hidden overlay basenames also include helper modules and potentially __init__.py.
findings.failure_mode: If a hidden overlay contains helpers.py, a valid agent-added src/helpers.py is deleted before grading. Likewise, an overlay __init__.py reserves that basename and can cause agent-added package initializers to be deleted. Correct solutions then fail imports or execute with altered package behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict removal to test modules that actually collide under pytest collection. Exclude package initializers and application/helper modules; account for package-qualified module names.

findings.description: Directory overlays are recognized in owned_dirs, but their Python files never contribute to reserved. Only overlays whose source is an individual file contribute hidden basenames.
findings.failure_mode: When a hidden suite is supplied as a directory overlay, an agent-added test with the same basename as a hidden test survives cleanup unless that basename independently occurs in fixture tests. Default pytest collection still aborts with an import-file-mismatch error, incorrectly failing a correct solution.
findings.suggested_fix: Recursively enumerate Python files inside directory overlays when building reserved, while preserving their destination paths as owned files.

findings.description: The reserved-basename set is far broader than the pytest failure it targets. It takes the basename of EVERY .py file under the fixture's tests/ or test/ directories (helpers.py, utils.py, factories.py, base.py ...) and of EVERY hidden-overlay .py file (the header itself names _oracle_x.py and helpers.py as sibling modules the hidden suites import), excluding only __init__.py and conftest.py from the fixture side (the overlay side does not even exclude __init__.py). It then sweeps the WHOLE tree, including source packages that do have __init__.py, and unlinks any agent-added file with a matching basename. pytest's 'import file mismatch' abort only affects modules pytest itself collects (python_files: test_*.py / *_test.py) that live in package-less directories; a helper module or a module inside a proper package never collides. So a feature-build/refactor agent that creates src/app/helpers.py or src/app/utils.py (very common names) while the fixture or hidden suite has tests/helpers.py or tests/utils.py has that module deleted before any command runs. The remaining code then raises ImportError and the hidden suite and regression suite both fail: a correct solution is graded as failing, which is precisely the mis-grade 1.2.11 claims to prevent, now triggered by a quieter path. The same rule also deletes fixture test files an agent legitimately relocated in a refactor task (new path not in fixture, basename reserved), silently shrinking the regression suite that regressions.final_green is computed from.
findings.failure_mode: Agent adds src/<pkg>/helpers.py (or utils.py, or any basename present under fixture tests/ or in the overlay). remove_colliding unlinks it in grading/final before the test command runs; hidden tests ImportError; hidden_test_pass_rate drops to 0 and regressions.final_green reads false for a correct solution. colliding_tests_removed hides this as a 'collision' and the only trace is grading/final.colliding-removed.txt.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict `reserved` to names pytest would actually collect: basenames matching the project's python_files patterns (default test_*.py and *_test.py; read pytest.ini/pyproject/setup.cfg if the fixture overrides them), and drop __init__.py from the overlay-derived set as well. Restrict the sweep to candidate files that pytest would import by bare basename, i.e. files in a directory with no __init__.py (walk up to the rootdir) or, simpler, only under the directories the task's test_command actually targets. Never remove a file whose directory contains __init__.py. Add a bats case asserting an agent-added src/<pkg>/helpers.py survives when the fixture has tests/helpers.py.

findings.description: `reserved` is built only from file overlays (`owned`); for a directory overlay (os.path.isdir(f)) the code records the dest prefix in `owned_dirs` to protect it from removal but never walks it to collect the .py basenames inside. A hidden suite delivered as a directory overlay therefore gets no collision protection at all, and the 1.2.11 guarantee ('removed before any command runs') does not hold for it: an agent tests/x/test_slug.py still aborts collection against the overlay's tests/hidden/test_slug.py.
findings.failure_mode: Task whose hidden tests are a directory overlay: agent-added test module with a hidden basename remains, pytest aborts with 'import file mismatch', correct solution graded as failing, colliding_tests_removed reports 0.
findings.suggested_fix: For each overlay entry where os.path.isdir(full), os.walk the source directory and add its .py basenames (minus __init__.py/conftest.py) to `reserved`, mirroring the fixture loop.

findings.description: The pre-flight refuses any present auth.json that has no tokens.access_token. The codex CLI also supports API-key mode, where auth.json holds OPENAI_API_KEY (and optionally auth_mode) with no tokens block; pipeline-run.sh copies such a file unchanged and the dissent would work fine, and KF-048 (single-use refresh token) does not apply to it. Under the new rule a host authenticated with an API key can never start a non-smoke batch, and the refusal text ('run codex login on the host') points to the wrong remedy.
findings.failure_mode: API-key-authenticated host: every fresh, --resume and --dry-run non-smoke batch is refused with 'has no tokens.access_token' although the codex voice would have run.
findings.suggested_fix: If `data` has no `tokens` block but has a non-empty OPENAI_API_KEY (or auth_mode == 'apikey'), record checked:false with a note and proceed instead of refusing; only treat a present but malformed `tokens` block as a refusal.

findings.description: required_until = now + 2 x (sum of the WHOLE plan's watchdog_s) / concurrency, and on --resume the already-completed trials are counted too. For the full 8-arm x 16-task x 3-trial suite this horizon is on the order of weeks; a batch with one trial left to resume demands the same token lifetime as a fresh batch. If the ChatGPT OAuth access token's lifetime is shorter than that horizon, no `codex login` can satisfy the check and there is no override flag, so non-smoke batches become unrunnable rather than merely degraded.
findings.failure_mode: Operator runs `codex login`, starts the batch, and is refused again with 'expires <ISO>, before the batch's required horizon <ISO>'; --resume of a nearly finished batch is refused for the same reason.
findings.suggested_fix: On --resume, sum watchdog_s only over trials without a row. Consider capping the horizon (e.g. at the token's typical lifetime) and downgrading an exp inside the horizon to a WARN plus a manifest note, or add an explicit --skip-codex-preflight that records checked:false.
